name: Purpose
description: Say why you are writing, in the first lines of the letter.

name: Background and history
description: Present the complaint and the relevant history.

name: Findings and results
description: Report examination findings, test results and the working diagnosis.

name: Treatment and progress
description: Describe what was done, how the patient responded and the plan.

name: Requests
description: Ask the reader clearly for what you need.

name: Closing
description: End the letter politely and mention enclosures.

name: Linking and signposting
description: Connect ideas so the letter reads as one clear case.

name: Opening
description: Greet, introduce yourself and explain the purpose of the conversation.

name: Gathering information
description: Ask open questions first, then closed ones; explore ideas, concerns and expectations.

name: Explaining
description: Explain medical matters in plain language, in small steps.

name: Empathy and reassurance
description: Show that you understand how the patient feels.

name: Agreeing a plan
description: Involve the patient in decisions and check they understand.

name: Closing
description: Summarise, invite questions and say what happens next.

name: Symptoms and signs
description: Formal terms for symptoms and clinical signs.

name: Clinical terms
description: Words for the course of disease and its treatment.

name: NHS roles and services
description: Who is who and where things happen in UK healthcare.

name: Hospital talk
description: What colleagues say on the ward, with the formal version for writing.

name: Everyday British English
description: Common informal expressions, with formal equivalents.
